LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down a touch, and while defense spending is still a steady tailwind, its profit margins have slipped below their usual mid-teens level, which is the one thing worth keeping an eye on here.

ASML.sentence: ASML edged higher again — it looks expensive if you only glance at last year's earnings, but the picture is more reasonable once you factor in the chip-machine demand expected to recover over the next couple of years.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — industrial gas demand is steady and they keep nudging prices up, though the stock is unusually priced right in line with its European rival Air Liquide rather than at its normal small premium.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — the shares have risen a bit but lagged their tech peers lately, while the AI cloud story just keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped a touch, but biotech funding is thawing out again, and since that money eventually turns into lab-equipment orders, it's an encouraging sign a few quarters out.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge slipped a little and pays a generous dividend, though its payout isn't quite as juicy relative to safe bonds as it gets when it's truly cheap — so it's fairly priced rather than a bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow fell again and is now well off its high, but it's still outrunning its software rivals as big companies and government agencies keep adopting its AI-automation tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore drifted down even as copper prices have been surging, which sets up a potential catch-up since this miner usually moves along with the metals it digs out.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta pulled back after its update, but the headline price-per-ton looked soft only because of the mix of products sold — strip that out and the price they get for their crushed stone is still climbing a healthy 3.7%, which is the part that actually matters.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is uneventful — the Mexican peso, which drives most of what this Latin American Coke bottler earns, is sitting in its normal range.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is barely moved, but with oil prices well above what it costs them to pump it out of the ground, they're generating plenty of cash to keep funding that hefty dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is flat this week, and the shares are priced below what it would cost to replace their fleet of container ships — a sign of long-term value in this global-trade bellwether.

MA.sentence: Mastercard eased down a little and is now priced right in line with Visa rather than at its usual small premium — nothing has actually changed in the business, people just keep tapping their cards.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company dropped and is down about a third from its high on general nervousness, even though there's no sign hospitals are using its machines any less.
